To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The proposed approach is a novel methodology that can be applied to any Recommender System, (ii) It is able to suggest papers that are not only similar to the user’s preferences, but also relevant to them, (iii) It is able for the first time to suggest papers that the user may be interested to read, based on his/her personal preferences, and (iv) It is a methodology that can be used in any domain.
1) The proposed system is a hybrid system that combines content-based filtering and collaborative filtering techniques.
1. The user is an integral component of the recommendation process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new Recommender System based on Multiple-Criteria Analysis (MCA).
the development of a new system that suggests scientific papers to a user based on his/her interests.
the design of an adaptive recommender system that takes into account the user’s profile and his preferences, as well as the content of the items.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed system is a good example of how a user-centric Recommender System can be built.
the proposed methodology is a promising approach to be considered as a new paradigm for the design of user-centric Recommender Systems.
the proposed methodology is a valuable contribution to the field, as it allows to provide personalized recommendations, taking into account the user’s preferences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a system is proposed for the recommendation of scientific papers.
the user is not anymore a passive recipient of recommendations but a proactive participant in the recommendation process, which is able to provide his/her opinion about the items suggested.

we have developed a new approach for Recommender Systems, based on Multiple Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) techniques and a user-centric model, that is capable to provide recommendations for a specific user, taking into account the user’s preferences and the user’s profile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed system is able to suggest papers to a user, taking into consideration the user’s preferences, the user’s profile and the papers’ profiles, as well.

the integration of a user’s profile in a Recommender System, through the use of Multiple Criteria Analysis, is able to improve significantly the recommendation results, by taking into account the user’s preferences and needs.

a user-centric Recommender System can be developed using a Multiple Criteria Analysis methodology, which allows for a better understanding of the user’s preferences, and thus, for a better recommendation of scientific papers.
